diffs.label: larmorx: 14 threads − 1 thread
diffs.reason: The same bytes at 1 and 14 threads: the replica divides the voxels between threads in fixed pieces, and the log-linear fit runs over each group at once as tedana's one lstsq call does.

diffs.label: larmorx: default − reproduce mode
diffs.reason: The default corrects TED-08, TED-05, NP-03, GLIBC-07 and names each where it changes a written value: 2,709 of 737,280 values change. TED-05: 14 voxels of the full T2* map more than ten times the cap, which tedana 26.0.x leaves uncapped (25.0.1 capped them), get the limited map's cap. NP-03: the log-linear fit's float32 log correctly rounded (numpy's own kernel is not); GLIBC-07: float64 exp, log and the curve fit's powers correctly rounded (glibc 2.35's are not): the curve fit starts from other last bits and ends within its tolerances elsewhere. `upstream_defects='reproduce'` gives tedana's outputs.

diffs.label: larmorx (replica) − fMRIPrep 25.2.6's own file (tedana 25.0.1)
diffs.reason: The replica is tedana 26.0.3 bit for bit, so this is tedana's own step from 25.0.1 (fMRIPrep's) to 26.0.3 (852 of 122,880 values): tedana 26.0.x caps only the limited T2* map (TED-05; 25.0.1 capped the full map, as larmorx's default does), loads the data as float32 (25.0.1: float64), applies the T2* floors to the full map and no longer clamps negative values; and fMRIPrep's image has other libraries (numpy 2.2.6, which sums more than 8,192 elements in chunks, SciPy 1.15.2, conda-forge's OpenBLAS). On this machine tedana 25.0.1 in fMRIPrep's image differs from tedana 26.0.3 in 2,660 values.

diffs.label: tedana: numpy's AVX-512 kernels on − off
diffs.reason: A reference row (the original against itself): numpy's float64 exp and log are Intel's SVML kernels on CPUs with AVX-512 (NP-04), glibc 2.35's otherwise; larmorx's reference is the path without them (decision D2): 2,061 of 737,280 values differ.
